Definition: Admah, a place near the Dead Sea
BiblicalUsage: Admah was one of the cities of the plain, named beside Sodom, Gomorrah, Zeboiim, and Bela. Its kings went to war against Chedorlaomer, and the city was destroyed with Sodom in the overthrow of the plain; the place itself is covered in the Biblical Places collection.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Admah's story is a mercy as much as a warning. God destroyed it, and then, speaking through Hosea, He says He will not do the same to His people — His heart recoils, His compassions are kindled, and judgment gives way to a love that refuses to let go.
